items.title: Diagnose why episode 0 stops at 17 steps with success=0
items.acceptance: Per-step action log identifies which agent emits action=0 and why
items.notes: Root cause: At step=2 a single bed detection (conf=0.888) crosses sem_threshold and locks found_goal=True. Its 3D back-projection writes a wrong target into object_pcd (truth distance 6.6m). For the next 14 steps the ShortestPathFollower drives the agent toward that incorrect 3D point. At step=17 the follower decides the goal is reached and returns 0; because found_goal is True, the override 'if not found_goal and action==0' does NOT trigger, so action=0 propagates to env.step and is_stop_called=True ends the episode. Recommended fixes: (a) require N-frame multi-confirmation before setting found_goal; (b) reset found_goal/object_pcd if proximity to nearest_point disagrees with detection; (c) raise --sem_threshold for synthetic+smoke scenes. Awaiting user choice.

items.title: Make flames penetrate smoke in the RGB sensor
items.acceptance: SmokeRGBSensor preserves flame pixels and adds a soft glow halo under dense smoke; HSV flame detector still fires on the smoke-attenuated RGB.
items.notes: Added flame_* knobs to SmokeRGBConfig (passthrough/glow/color bleed/HSV ranges). Rewrote SmokeRGBSensor: HSV flame mask + Gaussian glow boost transmittance T'=T+(1-T)*boost; surrounding smoke gets tinted by the local fire color; particulate noise is suppressed on the flame core. Verified with scripts/test_rgb_flame_through_smoke.py (flame mean RGB=240,111,44 vs bg 179,179,178 at density=0.9, 4 m) and scripts/test_flame_after_smoke.py (HSV detector returns one box, score 0.950).

items.title: Smoke-scene perception path: clean depth + smoky RGB + thermal
items.acceptance: Pipeline keeps Habitat clean depth for mapping, sources fire detections from thermal, and optionally dehazes the smoky RGB before YOLO-World.
items.notes: Added utils/smoke_perception.py (apply_clean_depth_and_thermal, dehaze_with_depth + estimate_smoke_k, thermal_mask_to_detections). Wired three new flags in arguments.py: --depth_use_clean (preserve clean depth obs), --use_thermal_perception (inject thermal channel + use thermal as fire source), --rgb_dehaze (depth-aware inverse Beer-Lambert + CLAHE). main.py and main_vec.py now call apply_clean_depth_and_thermal so observations carry smoky_rgb + clean_depth + thermal_image + thermal_flame_mask. Object_Detection_and_Segmentation.detect() takes thermal_flame_mask=...; when present, fire detections come from thermal (smoke-invariant) instead of HSV-on-smoky-RGB. vlm_agents/vlm_multi_agents pull obs['thermal_flame_mask'] and run the optional dehaze before transform_rgb_bgr. Validated via scripts/test_smoke_perception.py (apply/dehaze/thermal-detections all OK; bg dehazed from 179,179,179 to 150,151,151) and scripts/test_detect_with_thermal.py (gray RGB + thermal mask -> 1 fire detection conf 0.95). Existing tests test_flame_hsv.py and test_flame_after_smoke.py still pass under the project's co-nav env.

items.title: Run FireWorld voxel + Beer-Lambert RGB-D degradation together

items.notes: Added utils/fire_pipeline.compose_fire_step that runs FireWorldController.render_for_agent and FireSensorSuite.process on the clean RGB-D, then merges the outputs (FireWorld RGB + thermal + flame, suite depth_smoke + radar + lidar + dashboard) and patches observations in place. New flag --fire_world_compound_rgb stacks an extra global Beer-Lambert pass on top of the voxel RGB. main.py/main_vec.py replace the old if/elif with a single call. scripts/keyboard_teleop_fire.py gained --enable-suite/--smoke-density/--compound-rgb/--show-dashboard so the teleop window can show the voxel RGB while a second window shows the suite dashboard. Verified with a stub-driven smoke test (fw-only / suite-only / fw+suite all pass).

items.title: Refactor architecture: fire_world = world model, fire_sensors = observation
items.acceptance: fire_world only owns FireWorld + FireClock + FireScene; the voxel ray-march renderer + VoxelSmokeSensor live under fire_sensors; FireSensorSuite picks RGB/thermal source via cfg.rgb_source / cfg.thermal_source; legacy FireWorldController / FireWorldRenderer keep working through shims.
items.notes: Created utils/fire_world/scene.py (FireScene + FireClock + habitat_agent_state_to_cam). Trimmed utils/fire_world/runtime.py to host only FireWorld; FireWorldRenderer is now a back-compat shim that delegates to utils/fire_sensors/voxel_render.py. New utils/fire_sensors/voxel_render.py centralises the ray-march math and the volumetric_composite() entry point. New utils/fire_sensors/sensors/voxel_smoke.py wraps it as a BaseSensor. utils/fire_sensors/config.py gained VoxelSmokeConfig + rgb_source / thermal_source / compound_rgb. FireSensorSuite now accepts scene=FireScene + camera_K, instantiates VoxelSmokeSensor and uses it whenever rgb_source/thermal_source resolve to 'voxel'. utils/fire_pipeline.py shrank to a small step_fire_observation helper (compose_fire_step kept as alias). main.py / main_vec.py / scripts/keyboard_teleop_fire.py all rewritten around FireScene + FireSensorSuite. Verified by stub-driven tests (Beer-Lambert / voxel / voxel+compound) and by re-running the existing scripts/test_fire_world_step_clock.py against the real timeline.npz.

items.title: Voxel renderer: flame penetrates smoke; teleop dashboard layout fix
items.acceptance: Volumetric composite uses two transmittance accumulators so flame emission isn't eaten by smoke; teleop window shows RGB / Depth (smoke-degraded) / Thermal (INFERNO) instead of two depth-like panels.
items.notes: Added VoxelRenderParams.flame_smoke_passthrough (default 0.85). The marcher now keeps a separate T_acc_flame that uses (1-passthrough)*smoke_k + flame_k as the optical depth, so flame radiation leaks through smoke just like real visible-band fire imagery (Starr & Lattimer 2014 Fig. 7). Exposed via VoxelSmokeConfig + the legacy FireWorldRenderer shim. keyboard_teleop_fire.py now renders 3 panels (RGB / Depth-smoke / Thermal-INFERNO), forces thermal_color_blend=1.0 so it visually differs from JET-colored depth, always shows the suite's degraded depth (independent of --depth_use_clean), and exposes --flame-smoke-passthrough. Verified with a 1-ray micro test: with passthrough=0.0 a flame behind a smoke wall yields neutral grey RGB (R-B=0); with passthrough=0.85 the same configuration produces a warm tint (R=230, B=207). Existing scripts/test_fire_world_step_clock.py still passes against the real timeline.npz.

items.title: Fix flame visibility through smoke (teleop screenshot showed 2-pixel speck)
items.acceptance: Voxel-rendered flame is clearly visible behind dense smoke even with --compound-rgb=1; the second Beer-Lambert pass no longer erases the flame.
items.notes: Root causes: (a) flame_threshold=0.20 was higher than what trilinear interpolation yields at the flame envelope (0.05-0.30) so only the 0.6 source core survived as 1-2 pixels; (b) flame_emission_gain=4 was too low to penetrate dense smoke after attenuation; (c) compound_rgb=1 ran a second global Beer-Lambert that fogs flame pixels alongside everything else. Fix: lowered flame_threshold to 0.04 (and widened the smooth-step ramp to 0.05 above), bumped flame_emission_gain to 8.0, raised flame_smoke_passthrough default to 0.95, and added an optional flame_mask guard to _global_beer_lambert that blends the original voxel RGB back over flame pixels (with a Gaussian-dilated mask so the warm halo is preserved too). Quantified with a synthetic teleop-style scene (smoke wall in front of a 3x3x3 flame source): old defaults produced 0 warm pixels and max R-B=2; new defaults produce 24 warm pixels and max R-B=54; compound pass with the flame guard preserves all 24 pixels (without guard: 0).

items.title: Fix cross-numpy-version load failure in timeline.npz; restore staggered ignite times
items.acceptance: FireWorld.load works in conda env co-nav (numpy 1.24) regardless of which numpy wrote the npz; plan ignite_time_s values for the 4 new ignitions persisted.
items.notes: Root cause: propagation.py was saving meta as np.array([..], dtype=object) which forces pickle. The pickled string carried a numpy 2.x qualname (numpy._core), so loading under numpy 1.x raised ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'numpy._core'. Fix: write meta as a 0-d numpy unicode array under key 'meta_json' (no pickle), still emit the timeline_meta.json sidecar, and have FireWorld.load prefer the JSON sidecar -> meta_json -> legacy 'meta' (in that order) so old npzs keep loading too. Also: the kitchen/chair ignite_time_s values had reverted to 0; restored to 120/150/200/240. Reran propagation in /home/liushe10/miniconda3/envs/co-nav/bin/python so the cache is written by numpy 1.24 itself. Verified the new timeline reports first_flame at the expected timestamps for all 7 ignitions.

items.title: Author docs/fire_world_pipeline.md as the authoritative pipeline summary + paper-ready methodology
items.acceptance: docs/fire_world_pipeline.md walks through the 6 pipeline stages with implementation details and a self-contained methodology section that can be copied into a paper.
items.notes: Stage-by-stage write-up: (1) scene_scan with the sRGB OETF decode and per-face instance grouping, (2) planner templates + intensity presets + plan_id hashing, (3) reaction-diffusion-buoyancy-ceiling-jet voxel propagation, (4) FireScene runtime facade and the steps-per-unit / seconds-per-unit clock semantics, (5) FireSensorSuite voxel ray-march with dual-T flame channel + Beer-Lambert depth/radar/lidar/thermal, (6) integration into main.py / main_vec.py / keyboard_teleop_fire.py. Bottom half is a paper-ready methodology section with citations to Starr & Lattimer 2014 and a recommended ablation table. Appendix A is a file map; Appendix B is the minimal reproduction recipe.
